text_content:
When the experimental flag `` is enabled, Next.js expects a parent `` boundary around any component that awaits data that should be accessed on every user request. The purpose of this requirement is so that Next.js can provide a useful fallback while this data is accessed and rendered.
While some data is inherently only available when a user request is being handled, such as request headers, Next.js assumes that by default any asynchronous data is expected to be accessed each time a user request is being handled unless you specifically cache it using ``.
The proper fix for this specific error depends on what data you are accessing and how you want your Next.js app to behave.
